title: Lunar plume-surface interaction, dust mitigation and crew-exposure audit for OTA-TEC-0084
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0084 document. Using primary, peer-reviewed and official lunar mission/engineering sources, assess: (1) lunar regolith grain morphology, abrasion, adhesion and electrostatic charging; (2) Apollo observations of dust contamination and documented acute crew symptoms, while distinguishing them from unobserved or long-term diseases such as silicosis; (3) plume-surface interaction, erosion and ballistic ejecta from powered lunar landings, including uncertainty in ejecta quantities and vehicle self-contamination; (4) effects on seals, bearings, radiators, optics, engines and nearby infrastructure; (5) efficacy and maturity of prepared landing pads, dust-resistant materials, filtration, suitports/electrodynamic dust shields and other mitigation; and (6) whether the dossier's shorter maintenance interval relative to a Mars shuttle can be supported or must remain [H]. Identify wording that should be narrowed or reclassified. Do NOT evaluate or alter [F] fleet size, accident statistics, traffic frequency, ticket prices, fictional maintenance values, operators, Mars Credits, unlocks, journeys or any other NOXIA balancing value.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0084 makes lunar dust a dominant operational risk and the supplied early-NOXIA draft contained several overstrong statements; the corrected canonical version should now receive a source-pinned dust and human-exposure audit.
real_world_anchor: Apollo dust observations, NASA lunar dust health-risk work, plume-surface interaction research, lunar landing pad and dust-mitigation technology.
novelty_reason: First source-pinned lunar dust, plume interaction and crew-exposure audit of the canonical PELICAN technical object.
validation_summary: Der Kandidat ist ein quellengebundenes Realanker-Audit von OTA-TEC-0084-2026-DE (PELICAN) und bestaetigt saemtliche [R]-Anker des Dossiers (Kornmorphologie/Abrasion/Elektrostatik, Apollo-Reizsymptome ohne Silikose, PSI/Ejekta, Hardware-Wirkungen auf Dichtungen/Radiatoren/Optik) durch Primaer- und Peer-Review-Literatur; keine Retraktion, kein Materialwiderspruch, keine neue Kausalitaetsbehauptung. Damit ist kein conflict-Fall gegeben: die einzige materielle Spannung (Silikose-Angabe in OTA-TEC-0025 Abschnitt 4.3 gegen TEC-0084 und die NASA-Risikolage, ebenfalls Gegenstand dieses Kandidaten) ist bereits als EXT-KG-OTA-20260917-001 offen erfasst und wird hier nicht dupliziert; die vom Kandidaten ausdrueckliche Nicht-Hochstufung der Wartungskausalitaet zu [R] ist eine Bestaetigung, keine Aenderung.
